title: Claim Disk for Order Processor
description:
**SITUATION:**

Order Processor must write cold archives under `/data/archive` and keep them when Pods restart. The **platform team** already registered disk with the cluster (a PersistentVolume set aside for your lab). As the app team, you do **not** create that PV — you **claim** it by name on a PVC, then mount the claim into Order Processor.

[DevSetu Blog — Volumes, PVs, PVCs, and StorageClasses](/play/devops-engineer/kubernetes/read/volumes-pvs-pvcs-storageclasses)

**YOUR TASK:**

1. Find the platform **PersistentVolume** for your lab: list the PVs in the cluster and pick the one whose name **ends with your lab namespace** (`echo $LEARNER_NS` shows it).
2. Create a **PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC)** that **selects that PV** with `spec.volumeName` (plus matching size, access mode, and storage class).
3. **Update** the Order Processor Deployment so the container sees that storage at `/data/archive`.
4. Verify the claim is **Bound** to that PV and the Pod is **Ready**.

**SPEC:**

- PVC name: `order-archive-pvc`
- Access modes: `["ReadWriteOnce"]`
- Resources requests storage: `100Mi`
- `storageClassName`: `manual`
- `volumeName`: the platform PV you found in step 1 (pin it explicitly; do not rely on automatic matching alone)
- Deployment name: `order-processor-deploy` (do not rename)
- Replicas: set to **`1`** for this lab (this disk allows one writer — avoid two Pods fighting over it)
- Volume name in Pod: `archive`
- Mount path on `order-processor`: `/data/archive`
- Ready: PVC **Bound** to that PV; Deployment **1/1** Ready

**GOOD PRACTICES:**

- PVC in `order-archive-pvc-l19.yaml`; updated Deployment in `order-processor-pvc-l19.yaml`.
- Do **not** create or edit a PersistentVolume — select the one the platform already offered via `volumeName`.
- Work only in your lab namespace (not `default`).

hints: Your namespace is in the lab chrome and in $LEARNER_NS — kubectl already defaults there.
PVs are cluster-scoped: `kubectl get pv` lists every lab's disks. Yours is the one whose name ends with your namespace (`echo $LEARNER_NS`) — copy that exact name into the PVC's spec.volumeName.
Work only in your lab namespace (not default).
Read SPEC carefully, apply your YAML, then Submit.
problemStatement.solution:
# Solution — Claim Disk for Order Processor

Create PVC `order-archive-pvc` that **pins** the platform PersistentVolume with `volumeName`, then mount it into Deployment `order-processor-deploy` at `/data/archive`.

Docs: [DevSetu Blog — Volumes, PVs, PVCs, and StorageClasses](/play/devops-engineer/kubernetes/read/volumes-pvs-pvcs-storageclasses) · [PersistentVolumeClaims](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes/#persistentvolumeclaims)

## Discover the platform PV

The platform registered a cluster-scoped PV for your lab. PVs are not namespaced, so you will see other labs' PVs too; yours is the one whose name **ends with your namespace**:

```bash
echo "$LEARNER_NS"   # your lab namespace
kubectl get pv       # pick the PV whose name ends with it (STATUS Available)
```

## Solution YAML

Save as `order-archive-pvc-l19.yaml` (set `volumeName` to the PV you found):

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: order-archive-pvc
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 100Mi
  storageClassName: manual
  volumeName: <your-platform-pv-name>
```

Save as `order-processor-pvc-l19.yaml`:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: order-processor-deploy
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: order-processor
      version: v1.1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: order-processor
        version: v1.1
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: order-processor
          image: devsetu/order-processor:v1.1
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8000
          volumeMounts:
            - name: archive
              mountPath: /data/archive
      volumes:
        - name: archive
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: order-archive-pvc
```

## Declarative

```bash
kubectl apply -f order-archive-pvc-l19.yaml
kubectl apply -f order-processor-pvc-l19.yaml
kubectl get pvc order-archive-pvc
kubectl get pv   # your PV should now show STATUS Bound, CLAIM <namespace>/order-archive-pvc
kubectl get deploy order-processor-deploy
kubectl get pods -l app=order-processor -o wide
```

Wait until the PVC is **Bound** to that PV and the Deployment is **1/1 Ready**, then **Submit**.

Do **not** create or edit a PersistentVolume — select the platform one with `volumeName`, then mount the PVC. Work only in your lab namespace (not `default`).
